I had a very disappointing experience trying to get basic information from this clinic. I called to ask whether the doctor had experience treating tripod cats and could see mine if needed. I was asked to call back multiple times, and when I finally spoke with the receptionist, she was dismissive and condescending. Rather than answering a reasonable question, I was told “we don’t do that” and that I needed to see a specialist, without any medical context. I was not seeking advice just confirmation of the clinic’s capabilities before booking an appointment. The lack of professionalism and unwillingness to communicate respectfully is why I’m making a review to spread awareness to other tripod owners.

I am requesting to be contacted directly by the manager and, most importantly, the owner of this business.

I have verifiable evidence (calls and communications) regarding how certain non-medical staff members treat customers. To be clear, the doctors have been professional, but the behavior of some administrative staff is unacceptable.

On multiple occasions:
•	Our calls were hung up on
•	We were denied the opportunity to speak with a manager
•	When another person called specifically asking for a manager, they were placed on hold and then disconnected
•	We were given contradictory information, creating unnecessary confusion during a very sensitive situation

All of this occurred after payment had already been accepted, which makes the situation even more concerning.

Special mention to an employee named Lory / Loly (spelling uncertain):
My personal experience with her was extremely negative in terms of customer service. In my opinion:
•	Empathy: very low
•	Courtesy: poor
•	Communication: unclear and confusing

Additionally, I was incorrectly told that I was not allowed to record a phone call in which I am a participant, when in Texas this is legal. Providing incorrect legal information only escalated the situation unnecessarily.

Manager / Owner:
If you are genuinely interested in addressing and improving these practices, please provide an email contact. I am willing to share the relevant information and evidence directly and privately.

Situations involving medication and health should never be handled this way.

I am deeply disappointed by the lack of empathy and flexibility shown by "Lory," the employee who answers the phone. My dog, Pinky, is suffering from terminal cancer and urgently needs her pain medication.

Even though the prescription already exists, they refused to allow a trusted person to pick up the medication on my behalf simply because I am currently out of Texas. The payment was sent via Zelle, and they refuse to release the medication to me.

This decision directly impacts my dog's well-being and causes her unnecessary suffering. Pain management should never be delayed by rigid policies when reasonable solutions exist. Previously, family and friends have even picked up the medication for me, and we have proof of this.

Veterinary medicine is not just about rules, but about ethics, compassion, and prioritizing the animal's quality of life.

Unfortunately, this person, "Lory," failed to fulfill her responsibility. Previously, I've always received my medication, but "Lory" refused to give it to me, hung up on us repeatedly, and kept us on hold for over 20 minutes. She NEVER let us speak to a manager.

I hope no one else has to go through this, but "Lory" shouldn't work in customer service, especially when she doesn't meet the required standards. I've always sent someone to pick up my medication, and she's never denied it before.

This has truly been the worst vet I’ve ever been to in every way. My experience has been infuriating. The lady answering the phone is argumentative, incompetent, and lazy. The techs are nice but not knowledgeable enough to make up for Dr. Sudha Madhuri Yeddu’s poor bedside manner  and lack of attention to detail. See below if you want more info and warnings. I will never return here and you would be better off finding a place that actually cares about your pet.

1.  4 hour wait as a walk in
2.  Not a low cost clinic. That’s just the name. Only the office fee is lower than average. All testing and supplies seem to be quite average. And considering the lack of care, it is overpriced.
3. Do not come here if your cat has diabetes. They do not provide support. My vet refused to talk to me on the phone and instead look relayed messages through vet techs. I literally heard her talking to the vet to relay messages to me. So instead of answering my simple question the vet was trying to get me to come in for a full metabolic panel despite appetite not being the issue and having her bloodwork done days ago. Seems to just be trying to get money out of me.
4. They did not provide any information beyond “give insulin twice a day". No mention of what to do with dosing if the cat dislikes the food and doesn’t want to eat or skips a meal.
5. Didn’t ask if my cat had eaten the day I brought her in to better assess her current blood glucose level.
6. Did not recommend getting a glucometer and I had to ask an about it specifically. When I did ask about it the vet basically just said "sure you can get one, let us know what her BG is in two weeks".
Update:
7. Called to get a thyroid prescription refilled as it will run out before I can come in. I called and requested the refill online and was told I’d receive a call shortly after getting approval  from the doctor. I received no call back. I call the next day and was told that NO NOTE about the request could be found. I was told the doctor was out and I’d have to call back next business day. The lady on the phone was very argumentative and resistant to sending her a message of any sort. I called back again, again there was no note of my request, and I was finally told the doctor would not approve the refill because she may want to increase the prescription. I asked the lady on the phone to explain I can’t come in until the weekend and how the cat needs meds to get her through the week. The lady on the phone became irritable and argumentative and refused to talk to the doctor again for me. My cat will now have to miss multiple doses of medication because of the incompetence of the front desk staff.

In 2019, I brought my dog to this clinic because he had a mass on his neck that I was deeply concerned about. The veterinarian examined it and, without much discussion, decided to perform a needle aspirate. He was confident that it was likely pus-filled, but when he aspirated it, it turned out to be blood. I could tell by his expression that something was wrong, but no explanation was given. He simply let me leave without charging me, without providing any guidance on what had just happened, how to care for my dog, or what I should do next. There was no referral, no written record of the visit, and no advice on how to manage the bleeding that followed — nothing.

I went home and struggled alone to stop the bleeding, applying pressure and cold compresses for over an hour, crying and feeling helpless. Over time, my dog began developing lumps across his head and body. His abdomen became painful and distended. The mass he aspirated turned out to be hemangiosarcoma, an aggressive cancer that affected my dog’s spleen and began spreading rapidly throughout his body following that error. When my dog was finally properly diagnosed, he was only given two to four weeks to live. He passed in early 2020, just as predicted.

This experience has haunted me to this day. I trusted this clinic to help my dog, and instead I left with no answers and no support. I blame myself for his death. Had I’d known more back then about the types of cancer in dogs and how cancer spreads— I would’ve never let him poke my dog on a whim! But I depended on them for guidance and care and they let us both down in every way. I’m sharing this review nearly five years later because what happened to him was not okay. If I had only been charged for what happened, I’m sure I could have done something more about it, but I was young and didn’t know any better.
